title: Manicouagan Reservoir – The Eye of Quebec

beats.text: Enter the coordinates into a satellite map and you’ll spot a giant circular lake in Quebec.
From above the reservoir appears as a 70‑km‑wide ring of water surrounding a central island.
The shape has earned it the nickname “eye of Quebec”.
It is actually a 214‑million‑year‑old impact crater created by a 5‑km meteorite.
Inside lies René‑Levasseur Island, rising 952 m, and the lake holds 137.9 km³ of water.
That’s why the world refers to it as the eye of Quebec, visible from orbit.
Follow for more places you can see from space.

description: Manicouagan Reservoir in central Quebec covers 1,942 km² and is a 70‑km‑wide ring formed by a 214‑million‑year‑old meteorite impact. The central René‑Levasseur Island rises 952 m and the lake holds 137.9 km³ of water. Imagery: Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics. Photos: J-A Béland, CC BY-SA 4.0; NASA, Wikimedia Commons. Source: Wikipedia.
